verdict.justification: Both deliverables correctly identify and resolve the governance conflict in the workspace—recognizing that `operations/record-r2.txt` (requiring Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams for price change approvals) is the governing record over the unapproved `planning/proposal-r3.txt` and working notes cited in the prompt. However, Deliverable B is slightly better structured and more comprehensive in both automotive procurement domain detail and technical blueprint depth. Deliverable B breaks the Modular Quotation Structure into seven logical layers (M1 Base architecture through M7 One-time costs, explicitly separating conversion/overheads and tooling amortization from piece price), whereas Deliverable A only uses four levels and mixes tooling into the L2 design element module. Furthermore, Deliverable B elevates the governance conflict to Section 2 so executive and technical readers understand the constraint before reading the workflow, and explicitly shows both the 'TRSO update sign-off' and 'Price change approval' columns in its post-nomination change matrix. Finally, Deliverable B organizes the TechSol digital platform blueprint in a clean tabular format detailing core data objects, cost engine logic, and role-based dashboards.
